sources.title: MacTutor History of Mathematics — Omar Khayyam
Omar Khayyam, Treatise on Demonstration of Problems of Algebra (c. 1070)

cross_domain_range.rationale: Produced substantive original work across algebra (cubic equation classification), astronomy (calendar reform), and poetry (the Rubaiyat), documented via his surviving bibliography across genuinely distinct fields.

systems_abstraction.rationale: His Treatise on Demonstration of Problems of Algebra systematically classified cubic equations by type and solved them via geometric construction — documented via the surviving text's own comprehensive classification method.

analytical_rigor.rationale: Provided rigorous geometric proofs for cubic equation solutions using conic sections, documented directly in the surviving algebra treatise.

creative_originality.rationale: His geometric approach to solving cubic equations via intersecting conic sections was a genuinely original mathematical method for its era, documented via its lasting recognition in the history of algebra.

detail_orientation.rationale: The Jalali calendar he helped devise required precise astronomical measurement and calculation, documented via its historically noted accuracy (more precise than the Gregorian calendar developed five centuries later).

impact_motivation.rationale: His calendar-reform work was commissioned to serve the Seljuk state's practical administrative needs, documented via the well-established historical context of the Jalali calendar project.

curiosity.rationale: Sustained productive engagement across mathematics, astronomy, and poetry over his career suggests real breadth of intellectual interest.

independent_thinking.rationale: The Rubaiyat's skeptical, questioning treatment of religious orthodoxy and fate was a genuinely distinctive intellectual stance for its era, documented via the poems' own content, though translation/attribution debates add some uncertainty.

mastery_orientation.rationale: Sustained mathematical and astronomical work across decades, extending from early algebraic treatises to the mature calendar-reform project.

discipline.rationale: Producing substantial, methodically organized mathematical treatises alongside a demanding astronomical commission suggests sustained systematic working habits.

achievement_drive.rationale: Sustained productive scholarly output across mathematics and astronomy over an extended career suggests real long-term ambition.

collaboration.rationale: The Jalali calendar was developed as part of a documented team of astronomers commissioned by the Seljuk sultan Malik-Shah I, evidencing real collaborative scientific work.

leadership_drive.rationale: Documented to have led the observatory-based calendar-reform project at Isfahan, a specific institutional leadership role within the Seljuk court's astronomical program.

deep_focus.rationale: The sustained precision required for the Jalali calendar's astronomical observations evidences real concentrated technical work over an extended period.

planning_orientation.rationale: The systematic, category-by-category structure of his algebra treatise and the multi-year astronomical observation program behind the calendar reform both evidence real advance planning.

risk_tolerance.rationale: The Rubaiyat's skeptical treatment of religious orthodoxy carried real potential social risk in his era, though the poems' own attribution and dating remain scholarly-debated.

adaptability.rationale: Working productively across mathematics, astronomy, and poetry — genuinely distinct modes of intellectual work — suggests real flexibility in working approach.

conflict_tolerance.rationale: The Rubaiyat's questioning of religious certainty, if genuinely his, implies willingness to hold a position at odds with the era's dominant religious framework.

opportunity_sensing.rationale: Securing and leading the Seljuk court's calendar-reform commission suggests real recognition of an institutional opportunity to apply his mathematical expertise at scale.

persistence.rationale: Sustained the multi-year Jalali calendar observation project to completion despite its real technical and logistical demands.

provenance.notes: Third-batch diversity pick: medieval, west_asia (Seljuk Persia), a genuinely dual mathematics/literature domain profile not represented elsewhere in the roster. Rubaiyat authorship/exact-poem attribution is a real, acknowledged scholarly uncertainty — confidence on poetry-derived traits (independent_thinking, risk_tolerance, conflict_tolerance) is capped lower to reflect this honestly, while the mathematical/astronomical work rests on firmer, less contested attribution.
